'''Cliffton Nirgel Alexander'''<ref name="玉林晚报"/> (born November 16, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball player]] for the [[Guaiqueríes de Margarita]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (SPB). He completed his freshman season at the [[University of Kansas]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Jayhawks]]' on their [[2014–15 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2014–15 team]]. He declared himself eligible for the [[2015 NBA draft]] but was undrafted. He played one season for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and earned a second year of NBA service with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].

He played in high school at [[Curie Metropolitan High School|Curie High School]] in [[Chicago]] where he won [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|Naismith]] and [[Mr. Basketball USA]] recognition as [[List of U.S. high school basketball national player of the year awards|national player of the year]]. He did not play organized basketball until eighth grade, but by late in his freshman season he became a notable contributor to his high school's varsity team. He was ranked among the top 20 prospects in the national class of 2014 prior to his sophomore season. As a junior, he moved into the top 10 of the national class and was recognized as an All-American. By the beginning of his senior season, he was considered to be a top 5 player by most talent evaluators and his stock was still on the rise. Following a [[Martin Luther King Day]] performance during his senior year against the number one team in the country, many experts considered him to be the best player in the national class of 2014.

In 2013, he represented [[USA Basketball]] in international play. Several talent scouts praised his powerful game. As a high schooler, Alexander felt he was most often compared to [[Amar'e Stoudemire]]. He was also contrasted with crosstown rival [[Jahlil Okafor]], especially as a senior when they vied for national attention. Alexander was heavily recruited by many top [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] basketball programs and his recruitment was widely followed. He played in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], 2014 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and the 2014 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], earning co-MVP of the Jordan Brand Classic. Alexander led Curie to the 2014 [[Chicago Public High School League]] city championship in a quadruple-[[overtime (sports)|overtime]] game against Okafor that was the lead story on ''[[SportsCenter]]''. The championship was later forfeited. As a freshman with Kansas, he did not play in the latter part of the season after the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) launched an investigation into his eligibility.

==High school career==

===Freshman season===
Alexander, who was also a highly regarded football player, did not play organized basketball until eighth grade.<ref name=BrnCCAsp>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2011/05/03/basketball-recruiting-notes-curies-cliff-alexander-shows-promise-creighton-snags-crete-monees-michael-orris/|title=Basketball recruiting notes - Curie's Cliff Alexander shows promise|access-date=October 4, 2013|date=May 3, 2011|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}}</ref> Alexander played on Curie's 2010–11 varsity team as a freshman, but had little impact at first and sat out some games in December.<ref name=HRPPRPII>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2011/05/hoops_reports_player_power_ran_1.html|title=Hoops Report's Player Power Rankings: Part II|access-date=October 3, 2013|date=May 13, 2011|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130523122425/http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2011/05/hoops_reports_player_power_ran_1.html|archive-date=May 23, 2013}}</ref> He missed the first ten games due to a [[heart murmur]].<ref name=CAbar/> In late December, he started getting local attention as part of the reason Curie remained undefeated.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2010/12/holiday_hoops_primer_part_i.html|title=Holiday hoops primer: Part I|access-date=October 3, 2013|date=December 22, 2010|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004220143/http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2010/12/holiday_hoops_primer_part_i.html|archive-date=October 4, 2013}}</ref> During the [[Chicago Public High School League]] (CPL) and [[Illinois High School Association]] (IHSA) playoffs, he contributed significant performances.<ref name=HRPPRPII/> On March 9, 2011, Curie was eliminated from the IHSA playoffs in a Class 4A sectional semifinal by [[Lyons Township High School]] as freshman Alexander posted 9 [[point (basketball)|points]], 13 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 2 [[blocked shot|blocks]] in a 66–64 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2011/03/09/boys-basketball-4a-argo-sectional-nick-burts-layup-seals-lyons-victory-over-curie/|title=Boys basketball - 4A Argo Sectional: Nick Burt's layup seals Lyons' victory over Curie|access-date=October 5, 2013|date=March 9, 2011|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Hurst, Bob}}</ref> His late-season contributions gave Curie an added dimension,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2011/02/showdown_week_highlights_seaso.html|title=Showdown week highlights season|access-date=October 3, 2013|date=February 16, 2011|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130523112144/http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2011/02/showdown_week_highlights_seaso.html|archive-date=May 23, 2013}}</ref> as the team finished with a 28–3 record.<ref name=BrnCCAsp/> Following his freshman season, Alexander began to be recognized by local evaluators as a potential top national recruit.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2011/05/hoops_report_spring_cleaning.html|title=Hoops Report spring cleaning|access-date=October 3, 2013|date=May 30, 2011|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130523104355/http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2011/05/hoops_report_spring_cleaning.html|archive-date=May 23, 2013}}</ref> After [[Jabari Parker]] and [[Jahlil Okafor]], Alexander was already considered the best Chicago area basketball prospect.<ref name=HRPPRPII/> He earned Red-Central all-conference recognition.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.suntimes.com/schools/simeon/boys_basketball/4434712-566/public-league-all--conference-teams.html|title=Public League all- conference teams|access-date=October 5, 2013|date=March 23, 2011|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Travis, Clyde|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005075527/http://highschoolsports.suntimes.com/schools/simeon/boys_basketball/4434712-566/public-league-all--conference-teams.html|archive-date=October 5, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On September 8, 2016, Alexander signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-six-free-agents-training-camp-nick-johnson-cliff-alexander-damjan-rudez-20160908|title=Orlando Magic Sign Six Players|date=September 8, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 8, 2016}}</ref> but was later waived on October 16 after appearing in two preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-alexander-dawson-murphy|title=Magic Waive Alexander, Dawson, Murphy|work=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2016|access-date=October 16, 2016}}</ref> On October 29, he was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Magic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://erie.dleague.nba.com/16trainingcamp/|title=Nine Players Added to 2016 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031085138/http://erie.dleague.nba.com/16trainingcamp/|archive-date=October 31, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 22 games  he averaged 11.9 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.1 blocks in 24.5 minutes.<ref name="BayHawks">{{cite web|url=http://longisland.dleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-acquire-cliff-alexander/|title=Long Island Nets Acquire Cliff Alexander|work=NBA.com|date=January 31, 2017|access-date=February 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170203201306/http://longisland.dleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-acquire-cliff-alexander/|archive-date=February 3, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Long Island Nets (2017)===
On January 31, 2017, Alexander was traded to the [[Long Island Nets]] in exchange for a 2017 third-round draft pick.<ref name="BayHawks"/> On April 2, 2017, Alexander signed a 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. He was waived two days later before appearing in a game for the Nets. The 10-day contract had been guaranteed and earned Alexander a year of service (toward payscale minimums and pension eligibility) in the NBA making him a 2-year veteran.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/245515/Nets-Creatively-Honored-Agreements-With-Cliff-Alexander-Prince-Ibeh|title=Nets Creatively Honored Agreements With Cliff Alexander, Prince Ibeh|work=RealGM.com|date=April 4, 2017|access-date=April 5, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.nba.com/transactions/|title=NBA Transactions|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 5, 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Alexander's father is {{convert|6|ft|7|in|2|adj=on}} Clifton Terry, who played basketball for [[Paul Robeson High School (Chicago)|Robeson High School]] and [[Kennedy–King College]]. Following his time at the two-year Kennedy-King, Terry declared for the [[2001 NBA draft]]. His professional career included time in the [[NBA Development League]].
